parts: Lesson 19: Reading with Understanding: International Fight against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking — Summary

On the International Day against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking, the UN Secretary-General celebrates the millions who choose to live healthily and applauds those who have stopped using drugs. The message: 'Value yourself … make healthy choices.'

Nearly 200 million people still consume illegal drugs. Their names — crack, pot, junk, crystal meth, disco biscuits — sound colourful, but they are 'tickets to a dead end'. For addicts, choosing treatment is courageous and often life-saving. Those who have not ventured down this path should learn from those who have and firmly choose not to.
Healthy choices include a lifestyle good for body and mind, such as sports, which improve health and teach teamwork, discipline and self-confidence.

Addiction is a treatable disorder. Treatment tailored to individual needs lets patients lead normal, productive lives. Like diabetics or heart patients, they learn behavioural changes and often take medication: counselling, psychotherapy, support groups or family therapy; help against withdrawal and craving. Methadone in adequate doses with therapy reduces deaths and health problems from heroin.

The more treatment, the better the results; patients who stay longer do better, and those treated are likelier to have jobs and commit fewer crimes. The ultimate goal is lasting abstinence; the immediate goals are to reduce drug use, improve the patient's ability to function and minimise the medical and social harm.

Short-term methods (under six months): residential therapy, medication therapy, drug-free outpatient therapy. Longer-term: methadone maintenance outpatient treatment for opiate addicts, residential therapeutic communities.

illicit (not allowed by law), applaud (praise), trapped, venture (step into danger knowingly), regimen (a systematic plan), ultimate (main, final), lasting, adequate (enough), abstinence (staying away from drugs).
